I am farming here in Ruvuma on my own land, almost two hectares of maize, and the rains usually come well for us so I do not need to irrigate. I cannot afford much chemical fertilizer because the price is high and I have no schooling to help me read instructions on the bags, but I will put a small amount of urea as top dressing when the maize is knee-high, and I will spread manure from my few animals before planting. I will buy improved seed from the agro-dealer in town because my neighbors got better harvests with it last season, and I will spray a little pesticide if the fall armyworm comes like last year. My wife and older children will help me in the field, and during weeding and harvest I will call a few young men from the village to help for a small payment.
